Process

How a thumbnail earns the click

The same four checks, run on every project before it ships.

01

Hook

One clear idea a viewer can read in about two seconds — never two ideas competing for attention.

02

Contrast

Color and value separation strong enough to survive a tiny, scaled-down mobile feed.

03

Emotion

A face, reaction, or stake the viewer recognizes instantly — without needing the video's context.

04

Curiosity gap

Enough information to intrigue, never enough to fully resolve — that's what the click is for.

About

Design background, AI/ML mindset

I'm a first-year CSE (AI & ML) student who's spent the last two years building thumbnail design skills alongside coursework. That combination shapes how I work — every thumbnail is treated like a small experiment in attention, not just a pretty image.

I'm currently building toward full-time freelance thumbnail design, taking on practice briefs across tech, gaming, and mobile content while refining a consistent, repeatable process.
